---- MODULE W4Od5m4p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, QueueBound, PoolSize, MaxEpoch

ASSUME /\ QueueBound \in Nat /\ QueueBound > 0
       /\ PoolSize \in Nat /\ PoolSize > 0
       /\ MaxEpoch \in Nat /\ MaxEpoch > 0

VARIABLES sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ, casualQ, busyServers

vars == <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ, casualQ, busyServers>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ sessionEpoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ stampedAt \in [Players -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
  /\ rankedQ \subseteq Players
  /\ casualQ \subseteq Players
  /\ busyServers \in 0 .. PoolSize

Waiting == rankedQ \cup casualQ

QueuedTicketsAreCurrentAndUnique ==
  /\ \A p \in Waiting : stampedAt[p] = sessionEpoch
  /\ rankedQ \cap casualQ = {}

Init ==
  /\ sessionEpoch = 0
  /\ stampedAt = [p \in Players |-> 0]
  /\ rankedQ = {}
  /\ casualQ = {}
  /\ busyServers = 0

RotateEpoch ==
  /\ sessionEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ sessionEpoch' = sessionEpoch + 1
  /\ rankedQ' = {}
  /\ casualQ' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stampedAt, busyServers>>

RefreshToken(p) ==
  /\ stampedAt[p] < sessionEpoch
  /\ stampedAt' = [stampedAt EXCEPT ![p] = sessionEpoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, rankedQ, casualQ, busyServers>>

AdmitRanked(p) ==
  /\ stampedAt[p] = sessionEpoch
  /\ p \notin Waiting
  /\ Cardinality(rankedQ) < QueueBound
  /\ rankedQ' = rankedQ \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, casualQ, busyServers>>

AdmitCasual(p) ==
  /\ stampedAt[p] = sessionEpoch
  /\ p \notin Waiting
  /\ Cardinality(casualQ) < QueueBound
  /\ casualQ' = casualQ \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ, busyServers>>

StartRankedMatch(p) ==
  /\ p \in rankedQ
  /\ busyServers < PoolSize
  /\ rankedQ' = rankedQ \ {p}
  /\ busyServers' = busyServers + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, casualQ>>

StartCasualMatch(p) ==
  /\ p \in casualQ
  /\ busyServers < PoolSize
  /\ casualQ' = casualQ \ {p}
  /\ busyServers' = busyServers + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ>>

MatchFinishes ==
  /\ busyServers > 0
  /\ busyServers' = busyServers - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ, casualQ>>

Next ==
  \/ RotateEpoch \/ MatchFinishes
  \/ \E p \in Players :
       \/ RefreshToken(p) \/ AdmitRanked(p) \/ AdmitCasual(p)
       \/ StartRankedMatch(p) \/ StartCasualMatch(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Players = {plrA, plrB}
    QueueBound = 1
    PoolSize = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT QueuedTicketsAreCurrentAndUnique
nl:
A game studio runs two matchmakers side by side: the ranked matchmaker and the casual matchmaker. They were written by different teams, ship on different cadences, and know nothing about each other. What they share is one pool of game servers, and a server running a ranked match is a server that cannot run a casual one.

Each matchmaker keeps its own waiting queue, and each queue is bounded. When a queue is at its bound the matchmaker applies backpressure: it simply refuses to take another ticket until a match starts and a place frees up. The bound is what stops a queue growing without limit during an outage and then dumping thousands of stale tickets onto the pool when the outage clears.

Tickets are only as good as the session they were minted in. The account service stamps a session epoch on every player token, and rotates the epoch when it rolls a new authentication key -- after a credential leak, after a client patch, at the start of a season. A token stamped with an older epoch is stale, and a stale token is not a player the matchmakers may act on. Rotating the epoch therefore empties both waiting queues in the same motion, because everything sitting in them was admitted on the strength of a token that no longer means anything. A player whose token has gone stale refreshes it against the current epoch and can then queue again.

The one thing neither matchmaker can check for itself is whether the other has already taken a player, so the studio enforces it at the point of admission: a player is only admitted to a queue if they are in neither queue at that moment.

The actions of the system are: the account service rotating the session epoch and emptying both queues, a player refreshing a stale token against the current epoch, admitting a current-token player who is in neither queue to the ranked queue while it is under its bound, admitting such a player to the casual queue while it is under its bound, starting a ranked match on a free server and taking that player off the ranked queue, starting a casual match on a free server and taking that player off the casual queue, and a match finishing and releasing its server.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every player sitting in either waiting queue holds a token stamped with the current session epoch, and no player is in both queues at once.

---- MODULE W4Od14m4p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS DroneOne, DroneTwo, QueueBound, MaxPreempts, NoDrone

Drones == {DroneOne, DroneTwo}

ASSUME /\ DroneOne # DroneTwo
       /\ NoDrone \notin Drones
       /\ QueueBound \in Nat /\ QueueBound > 0
       /\ MaxPreempts \in Nat

VARIABLES uplink, sending, buffered, asking, preemptsLeft

vars == <<uplink, sending, buffered, asking, preemptsLeft>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ uplink \in Drones \cup {NoDrone}
  /\ sending \subseteq Drones
  /\ buffered \in [Drones -> 0 .. QueueBound]
  /\ asking \subseteq Drones
  /\ preemptsLeft \in 0 .. MaxPreempts

OnlyTheUplinkHolderTransmits ==
  /\ sending \subseteq {uplink}
  /\ \A d \in sending : buffered[d] > 0

Init ==
  /\ uplink = NoDrone
  /\ sending = {}
  /\ buffered = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ asking = {}
  /\ preemptsLeft = MaxPreempts

BufferFrame(d) ==
  /\ buffered[d] < QueueBound
  /\ buffered' = [buffered EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<uplink, sending, asking, preemptsLeft>>

AskForUplink(d) ==
  /\ buffered[d] > 0
  /\ d \notin asking
  /\ asking' = asking \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<uplink, sending, buffered, preemptsLeft>>

GrantUplink(d) ==
  /\ uplink = NoDrone
  /\ d \in asking
  /\ uplink' = d
  /\ asking' = asking \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sending, buffered, preemptsLeft>>

KeyTransmitter(d) ==
  /\ uplink = d
  /\ d \notin sending
  /\ buffered[d] > 0
  /\ sending' = sending \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<uplink, buffered, asking, preemptsLeft>>

DrainFrame(d) ==
  /\ d \in sending
  /\ buffered[d] > 1
  /\ buffered' = [buffered EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<uplink, sending, asking, preemptsLeft>>

StopAndRelease(d) ==
  /\ uplink = d
  /\ sending' = sending \ {d}
  /\ uplink' = NoDrone
  /\ UNCHANGED <<buffered, asking, preemptsLeft>>

CommanderPreempts(d) ==
  /\ preemptsLeft > 0
  /\ uplink # NoDrone
  /\ uplink # d
  /\ uplink' = d
  /\ sending' = {}
  /\ asking' = asking \ {d}
  /\ preemptsLeft' = preemptsLeft - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED buffered

Next ==
  \E d \in Drones :
    \/ BufferFrame(d) \/ AskForUplink(d) \/ GrantUplink(d)
    \/ KeyTransmitter(d) \/ DrainFrame(d) \/ StopAndRelease(d)
    \/ CommanderPreempts(d)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(StopAndRelease(DroneOne))
  /\ WF_vars(StopAndRelease(DroneTwo))

TransmissionsAlwaysEnd ==
  \A d \in Drones : (d \in sending) ~> (d \notin sending)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    DroneOne = droneOne
    DroneTwo = droneTwo
    QueueBound = 2
    MaxPreempts = 1
    NoDrone = noDrone
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheUplinkHolderTransmits
PROPERTY TransmissionsAlwaysEnd
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm carries one satellite uplink between all of its drones. The uplink is a single radio: two drones keying it at the same time produce a collision that costs the ground station the whole pass, so exactly one drone may be transmitting at any instant, and only the drone that currently holds the uplink may transmit at all.

Imagery comes off the sensors faster than the uplink can carry it, so each drone buffers frames into a bounded outbound queue. When a drone's queue is full it applies backpressure and stops accepting frames from its own sensor rather than overwriting what is already buffered -- a dropped frame in the middle of a burn perimeter is worse than a gap at the end of it. A drone with nothing buffered has no reason to want the uplink; a drone with frames buffered asks for it and waits its turn.

Holding the uplink is a three-step affair: a waiting drone is granted the uplink, keys the transmitter and starts sending, and then stops sending and gives the uplink back when its buffer has drained enough. The grant is what makes the exclusion work: a drone that has not been granted the uplink never keys the transmitter.

The incident commander can preempt. When a spotter drone has line of sight on a new head of fire, the commander takes the uplink away from whoever has it -- stopping that drone's transmission in the same motion -- and gives it to the drone that matters. Preemption is rationed for the flight, because every preemption is a truncated frame somebody has to re-fly.

The actions of the system are: a drone buffering a frame from its own sensor while its queue is under its bound, a drone with frames buffered asking for the uplink, granting the uplink to a waiting drone, the holder keying the transmitter and starting to send, the holder stopping and giving the uplink back, a drone draining one frame out of its buffer while transmitting, and the incident commander preempting the uplink away from whoever holds it and stopping that drone's transmission.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of drones transmitting is always contained in the set containing just the drone that currently holds the uplink, so two drones never key the radio at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A drone that has started transmitting eventually stops transmitting, whether it finishes on its own or the incident commander preempts it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m0p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drivers, Columns, MaxFacings, MaxGen, NoColumn

ASSUME /\ NoColumn \notin Columns
       /\ MaxFacings \in Nat /\ MaxFacings > 0
       /\ MaxGen \in Nat /\ MaxGen > 0

VARIABLES stock, facings, planGen, claimOn, notedGen

vars == <<stock, facings, planGen, claimOn, notedGen>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ stock \in [Columns -> 0 .. MaxFacings]
  /\ facings \in [Columns -> 1 .. MaxFacings]
  /\ planGen \in 0 .. MaxGen
  /\ claimOn \in [Drivers -> Columns \cup {NoColumn}]
  /\ notedGen \in [Drivers -> 0 .. MaxGen]

Claiming == {d \in Drivers : claimOn[d] # NoColumn}

StockFitsTheFacings ==
  /\ \A c \in Columns : stock[c] <= facings[c]
  /\ \A d \in Claiming : notedGen[d] <= planGen

Init ==
  /\ stock = [c \in Columns |-> 0]
  /\ facings = [c \in Columns |-> MaxFacings]
  /\ planGen = 0
  /\ claimOn = [d \in Drivers |-> NoColumn]
  /\ notedGen = [d \in Drivers |-> 0]

OpenClaim(d, c) ==
  /\ claimOn[d] = NoColumn
  /\ claimOn' = [claimOn EXCEPT ![d] = c]
  /\ notedGen' = [notedGen EXCEPT ![d] = planGen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, facings, planGen>>

Restock(d) ==
  /\ claimOn[d] # NoColumn
  /\ notedGen[d] = planGen
  /\ stock[claimOn[d]] < facings[claimOn[d]]
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![claimOn[d]] = @ + 1]
  /\ claimOn' = [claimOn EXCEPT ![d] = NoColumn]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<facings, planGen, notedGen>>

AbandonStale(d) ==
  /\ claimOn[d] # NoColumn
  /\ notedGen[d] # planGen
  /\ claimOn' = [claimOn EXCEPT ![d] = NoColumn]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, facings, planGen, notedGen>>

AbandonFull(d) ==
  /\ claimOn[d] # NoColumn
  /\ notedGen[d] = planGen
  /\ stock[claimOn[d]] = facings[claimOn[d]]
  /\ claimOn' = [claimOn EXCEPT ![d] = NoColumn]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, facings, planGen, notedGen>>

Republish(f) ==
  /\ planGen < MaxGen
  /\ f \in [Columns -> 1 .. MaxFacings]
  /\ \A c \in Columns : f[c] >= stock[c]
  /\ facings' = f
  /\ planGen' = planGen + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, claimOn, notedGen>>

Purchase(c) ==
  /\ stock[c] > 0
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<facings, planGen, claimOn, notedGen>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in [Columns -> 1 .. MaxFacings] : Republish(f)
  \/ \E c \in Columns : Purchase(c)
  \/ \E d \in Drivers :
       \/ Restock(d) \/ AbandonStale(d) \/ AbandonFull(d)
       \/ \E c \in Columns : OpenClaim(d, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Drivers = {routeDrvA, routeDrvB}
    Columns = {colA, colB}
    MaxFacings = 2
    MaxGen = 2
    NoColumn = noColumn
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT StockFitsTheFacings
nl:
A vending operator's machines hold their product in columns, and each column has a number of facings -- how many units of that product physically fit in it. Route drivers restock the columns from handhelds, with no lock anywhere: a driver opens a claim against a column, notes the planogram generation the machine was running when the claim was opened, and restocks only if the machine is still running that generation.

The planogram is the thing that changes underneath them. Head office republishes it during the day as promotions start and finish, and republishing sets new facings for every column at once and advances the generation. Facings can go down as well as up -- a column that was three facings of one drink becomes two of another -- but head office may never publish facings below what a column is already holding, because there is nowhere for displaced units to go and pulling stock back out of a machine is a separate, audited job.

A driver whose claim was opened against an older generation is working from a planogram that no longer applies, and abandons the claim rather than restocking against it. A driver whose claim is current but whose column is already full to its facings also abandons, since there is nothing to put in. Customers buying product take units out of columns and are what makes room again.

The actions of the system are: a driver opening a claim against a column and noting the current planogram generation, a driver restocking one unit into a column whose noted generation still matches and which is under its facings, a driver abandoning a claim whose noted generation no longer matches, a driver abandoning a current claim on a column that is already full to its facings, head office republishing the planogram with new facings no lower than what each column already holds, and a customer buying a unit out of a column.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No column ever holds more units than its current facings, and no driver's open claim was noted against a planogram generation ahead of the one in force.

---- MODULE W4Od12m0p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS TechOne, TechTwo, Units, MaxClock, MaxRev, NoUnit

Techs == {TechOne, TechTwo}

ASSUME /\ TechOne # TechTwo
       /\ NoUnit \notin Units
       /\ MaxClock \in Nat /\ MaxRev \in Nat

VARIABLES auditClock, certTo, postingOn, notedRev, rev

vars == <<auditClock, certTo, postingOn, notedRev, rev>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ auditClock \in 0 .. MaxClock
  /\ certTo \in [Techs -> 0 .. MaxClock]
  /\ postingOn \in [Techs -> Units \cup {NoUnit}]
  /\ notedRev \in [Techs -> 0 .. MaxRev]
  /\ rev \in [Units -> 0 .. MaxRev]

Open == {t \in Techs : postingOn[t] # NoUnit}

OpenPostingsAreCertifiedAndSane ==
  /\ \A t \in Open : certTo[t] >= auditClock
  /\ \A t \in Open : notedRev[t] <= rev[postingOn[t]]

Init ==
  /\ auditClock = 0
  /\ certTo = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
  /\ postingOn = [t \in Techs |-> NoUnit]
  /\ notedRev = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
  /\ rev = [u \in Units |-> 0]

AdvanceClock ==
  /\ auditClock < MaxClock
  /\ auditClock' = auditClock + 1
  /\ postingOn' = [t \in Techs |->
                     IF certTo[t] < auditClock + 1 THEN NoUnit ELSE postingOn[t]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<certTo, notedRev, rev>>

Recertify(t) ==
  /\ certTo[t] < MaxClock
  /\ certTo' = [certTo EXCEPT ![t] = MaxClock]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, postingOn, notedRev, rev>>

OpenPosting(t, u) ==
  /\ certTo[t] >= auditClock
  /\ postingOn[t] = NoUnit
  /\ postingOn' = [postingOn EXCEPT ![t] = u]
  /\ notedRev' = [notedRev EXCEPT ![t] = rev[u]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, certTo, rev>>

WritePosting(t) ==
  /\ certTo[t] >= auditClock
  /\ postingOn[t] # NoUnit
  /\ notedRev[t] = rev[postingOn[t]]
  /\ rev[postingOn[t]] < MaxRev
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![postingOn[t]] = @ + 1]
  /\ postingOn' = [postingOn EXCEPT ![t] = NoUnit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, certTo, notedRev>>

ReRead(t) ==
  /\ postingOn[t] # NoUnit
  /\ notedRev[t] # rev[postingOn[t]]
  /\ notedRev' = [notedRev EXCEPT ![t] = rev[postingOn[t]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, certTo, postingOn, rev>>

CloseAtCeiling(t) ==
  /\ postingOn[t] # NoUnit
  /\ rev[postingOn[t]] = MaxRev
  /\ postingOn' = [postingOn EXCEPT ![t] = NoUnit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, certTo, notedRev, rev>>

Clears(t) == WritePosting(t) \/ ReRead(t) \/ CloseAtCeiling(t)

Next ==
  \/ AdvanceClock
  \/ \E t \in Techs :
       \/ Clears(t) \/ Recertify(t)
       \/ \E u \in Units : OpenPosting(t, u)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Clears(TechOne))
  /\ WF_vars(Clears(TechTwo))

OpenPostingsAlwaysClose ==
  \A t \in Techs : (postingOn[t] # NoUnit) ~> (postingOn[t] = NoUnit)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    TechOne = bankTechOne
    TechTwo = bankTechTwo
    Units = {unitA, unitB}
    MaxClock = 2
    MaxRev = 2
    NoUnit = noUnit
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OpenPostingsAreCertifiedAndSane
PROPERTY OpenPostingsAlwaysClose
nl:
A blood bank's inventory records are posted to by technicians working without any lock on the record. A technician opens a posting against a unit record, notes the revision the record was on, and writes only if the record is still on that revision; if it has moved, the technician re-reads and works from the new revision instead.

Who may post is governed by the competency register. Every technician's competency is certified to a particular point on the bank's audit clock, and the clock advances as the day's audit windows close. A technician whose certification point is behind the clock is out of certification and may not post to anything. The bank is strict about this because a posting made by an uncertified technician has to be backed out by hand and every unit it touched has to be re-tested. When the clock advances past a technician's certification point, any posting that technician had open is closed out in the same motion -- the posting cannot be allowed to sit there and land later. Technicians re-certify against the register and can then post again.

Technicians here are slow, not broken. A technician is interrupted by a cross-match, a phone call from theatre, a courier at the door; a posting can sit open across several clock advances while the record underneath it moves on. That is what the re-read is for, and it is why the certification check has to be made again at the moment of writing rather than only when the posting was opened.

Unit records stop accepting postings once they reach the revision ceiling the bank keeps for a single audit day; a technician holding a posting against a record at the ceiling closes it out rather than re-reading forever.

The actions of the system are: the audit clock advancing and closing out the postings of every technician whose certification is now behind it, a technician re-certifying against the register, a certified technician opening a posting against a unit record and noting its revision, a certified technician writing a posting whose noted revision still matches and advancing the record, a technician re-reading a record whose revision moved underneath its open posting, and a technician closing out a posting against a record that has reached the day's revision ceiling.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every technician with a posting open is certified to a point at or beyond the current audit clock, and no open posting was noted against a revision ahead of the one its record is actually on.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A technician with a posting open eventually has no posting open, whether it is written, closed out at the ceiling, or closed out when the clock passes that technician's certification.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m3p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, Blocks, MaxTerm, MaxOverrides, NoNode

ASSUME /\ NoNode \notin Nodes
       /\ Blocks \in Nat /\ Blocks > 0
       /\ MaxTerm \in Nat /\ MaxTerm > 0

VARIABLES seat, term, served, shedded, spare, overridesLeft

vars == <<seat, term, served, shedded, spare, overridesLeft>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ seat \in Nodes \cup {NoNode}
  /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
  /\ served \in 0 .. Blocks
  /\ shedded \in 0 .. Blocks
  /\ spare \in 0 .. Blocks
  /\ overridesLeft \in 0 .. MaxOverrides

DemandBlocksAreConserved == served + shedded + spare = Blocks

Init ==
  /\ seat = NoNode
  /\ term = 0
  /\ served = Blocks
  /\ shedded = 0
  /\ spare = 0
  /\ overridesLeft = MaxOverrides

ElectCoordinator(n) ==
  /\ seat = NoNode
  /\ seat' = n
  /\ term' = IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE term
  /\ UNCHANGED <<served, shedded, spare, overridesLeft>>

CoordinatorFalls ==
  /\ seat # NoNode
  /\ seat' = NoNode
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, served, shedded, spare, overridesLeft>>

ShedBlock ==
  /\ seat # NoNode
  /\ served > 0
  /\ served' = served - 1
  /\ shedded' = shedded + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, spare, overridesLeft>>

RestoreBlock ==
  /\ seat # NoNode
  /\ shedded > 0
  /\ shedded' = shedded - 1
  /\ served' = served + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, spare, overridesLeft>>

CommissionSpare ==
  /\ seat # NoNode
  /\ spare > 0
  /\ spare' = spare - 1
  /\ served' = served + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, shedded, overridesLeft>>

TakeForMaintenance ==
  /\ served > 0
  /\ served' = served - 1
  /\ spare' = spare + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, shedded, overridesLeft>>

OperatorOverride ==
  /\ overridesLeft > 0
  /\ served > 0
  /\ served' = served - 1
  /\ shedded' = shedded + 1
  /\ overridesLeft' = overridesLeft - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, spare>>

Next ==
  \/ CoordinatorFalls \/ ShedBlock \/ RestoreBlock \/ CommissionSpare
  \/ TakeForMaintenance \/ OperatorOverride
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : ElectCoordinator(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {shedNodeA, shedNodeB}
    Blocks = 3
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxOverrides = 1
    NoNode = noNode
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DemandBlocksAreConserved
nl:
A regional power grid runs an automatic load shedder over a fixed block of demand. The demand is measured in whole blocks and the number of blocks is fixed for the interval: the shedder does not create demand and it does not destroy it, it only moves blocks between three states. A block is either being served, or shed, or held in spare -- capacity that is committed to nothing at this instant and is available to be commissioned into service.

The shedder is driven by one coordinator node at a time. The nodes elect a coordinator and the election stamps a term number on the winner, up to the highest term the interval's register can record. A coordinator that falls over leaves the seat empty and the shedder does nothing at all until a new election fills it; every ordinary shedding decision goes through the seated coordinator.

The decisions are the obvious ones. The coordinator sheds a served block, which moves it from served to shed. It restores a shed block, which moves it back from shed to served. It commissions a spare block into service, moving it from spare to served. Blocks also come out of service back to spare when a feeder is taken off for maintenance, which is a field operation and does not need the coordinator.

The system operator has an override for the seconds when frequency is falling and there is no coordinator seated: the operator sheds a served block directly. The override is rationed for the interval and each use is written into the disturbance report. It moves a block from served to shed exactly like an ordinary shed does -- what it skips is the coordinator, not the accounting.

The actions of the system are: electing a coordinator and advancing the term, the coordinator falling over and leaving the seat empty, the coordinator shedding a served block, the coordinator restoring a shed block to service, the coordinator commissioning a spare block into service, a feeder being taken off for maintenance so a served block goes back to spare, and the system operator overriding to shed a served block directly.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The blocks being served, the blocks shed and the blocks held in spare always sum to exactly the fixed number of demand blocks in the interval.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m7p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS CarOne, CarTwo, Pax, MaxCap, MaxGen

Cars == {CarOne, CarTwo}

ASSUME /\ CarOne # CarTwo
       /\ MaxCap \in Nat /\ MaxCap > 0
       /\ MaxGen \in Nat /\ MaxGen > 0

VARIABLES lobby, riding, delivered, regGen, notedGen, capacity

vars == <<lobby, riding, delivered, regGen, notedGen, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ lobby \subseteq Pax
  /\ riding \in [Cars -> SUBSET Pax]
  /\ delivered \subseteq Pax
  /\ regGen \in 0 .. MaxGen
  /\ notedGen \in [Cars -> 0 .. MaxGen]
  /\ capacity \in 1 .. MaxCap

Aboard == riding[CarOne] \cup riding[CarTwo]

PassengersArePartitioned ==
  /\ lobby \cup Aboard \cup delivered = Pax
  /\ lobby \cap Aboard = {}
  /\ lobby \cap delivered = {}
  /\ Aboard \cap delivered = {}
  /\ riding[CarOne] \cap riding[CarTwo] = {}

Init ==
  /\ lobby = Pax
  /\ riding = [c \in Cars |-> {}]
  /\ delivered = {}
  /\ regGen = 0
  /\ notedGen = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ capacity = MaxCap

ReReadRegister(c) ==
  /\ notedGen[c] # regGen
  /\ notedGen' = [notedGen EXCEPT ![c] = regGen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, riding, delivered, regGen, capacity>>

Board(c, p) ==
  /\ notedGen[c] = regGen
  /\ regGen < MaxGen
  /\ p \in lobby
  /\ Cardinality(riding[c]) < capacity
  /\ lobby' = lobby \ {p}
  /\ riding' = [riding EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {p}]
  /\ regGen' = regGen + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<delivered, notedGen, capacity>>

EmptyCar(c) ==
  /\ riding[c] # {}
  /\ delivered' = delivered \cup riding[c]
  /\ riding' = [riding EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, regGen, notedGen, capacity>>

RetuneCapacity(n) ==
  /\ n \in 1 .. MaxCap
  /\ \A c \in Cars : Cardinality(riding[c]) <= n
  /\ capacity' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, riding, delivered, regGen, notedGen>>

ReturnToLobby(p) ==
  /\ p \in delivered
  /\ delivered' = delivered \ {p}
  /\ lobby' = lobby \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<riding, regGen, notedGen, capacity>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxCap : RetuneCapacity(n)
  \/ \E p \in Pax : ReturnToLobby(p)
  \/ \E c \in Cars :
       \/ ReReadRegister(c) \/ EmptyCar(c)
       \/ \E p \in Pax : Board(c, p)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(EmptyCar(CarOne))
  /\ WF_vars(EmptyCar(CarTwo))

CarsAlwaysEmpty ==
  \A c \in Cars : (riding[c] # {}) ~> (riding[c] = {})

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    CarOne = elevCarOne
    CarTwo = elevCarTwo
    Pax = {paxA, paxB}
    MaxCap = 2
    MaxGen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PassengersArePartitioned
PROPERTY CarsAlwaysEmpty
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank tracks where every passenger in the system is. A passenger is in exactly one of three places: waiting in the lobby, riding inside exactly one car, or already delivered to a floor. Nobody is ever counted in two places and nobody drops off the roll -- the building's evacuation board is printed off this record, and a passenger who is on it twice or not at all is a passenger the fire service will go looking for in the wrong place.

Boarding is coordinated through a single assignment register that the cars share, using compare-and-swap rather than a lock, because a car cannot afford to wait on a lock while its doors are open. A car reads the register's generation, and boarding only goes ahead if the register is still on that generation when the passenger actually steps in; a successful board advances the generation, which is what makes the other car's read stale. A car whose read has gone stale simply re-reads the register.

Car capacity is not a constant. The building manager retunes it during the day -- a lower figure while a goods move is running and the cars are sharing the shafts with pallets, a higher figure at end of shift. Capacity may be lowered as well as raised, but never below what a car is already carrying, because there is no way to put a passenger back in the lobby out of a moving car. Boarding is only allowed while the boarding car is under its capacity as it stands at that moment.

A car empties at its destination: everybody riding it is delivered in one motion and the car is empty again. Delivered passengers make return trips, coming back into the lobby to wait for another car, which is why the roll never stops moving.

The actions of the system are: a car re-reading the assignment register when its noted generation has gone stale, a car boarding a waiting passenger while its read is current and it is under capacity, which advances the register, a car emptying and delivering everybody riding it, the building manager retuning car capacity to a figure not below what any car is carrying, and a delivered passenger returning to the lobby.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The passengers waiting in the lobby, the passengers riding each car and the passengers already delivered partition the whole set of passengers, with nobody in two places and nobody in none.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A car that has passengers riding it eventually has none, because every car empties at its destination.

---- MODULE W4Od19m0p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Stations, Titles, ShelfSize, Slack, MaxRev, NoTitle

ASSUME /\ NoTitle \notin Titles
       /\ ShelfSize \in Nat /\ ShelfSize > 0
       /\ Slack \in Nat /\ Slack > 0
       /\ MaxRev \in Nat /\ MaxRev > 0

VARIABLES onShelf, rev, attemptOn, notedRev, dead

vars == <<onShelf, rev, attemptOn, notedRev, dead>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ onShelf \in [Titles -> 0 .. ShelfSize + Slack]
  /\ rev \in [Titles -> 0 .. MaxRev]
  /\ attemptOn \in [Stations -> Titles \cup {NoTitle}]
  /\ notedRev \in [Stations -> 0 .. MaxRev]
  /\ dead \subseteq Stations

ShelvesFitAndDeadStationsHoldNothing ==
  /\ \A t \in Titles : onShelf[t] <= ShelfSize
  /\ \A s \in dead : attemptOn[s] = NoTitle

Init ==
  /\ onShelf = [t \in Titles |-> 0]
  /\ rev = [t \in Titles |-> 0]
  /\ attemptOn = [s \in Stations |-> NoTitle]
  /\ notedRev = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
  /\ dead = {}

OpenAttempt(s, t) ==
  /\ s \notin dead
  /\ attemptOn[s] = NoTitle
  /\ attemptOn' = [attemptOn EXCEPT ![s] = t]
  /\ notedRev' = [notedRev EXCEPT ![s] = rev[t]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, rev, dead>>

PostHold(s) ==
  /\ s \notin dead
  /\ attemptOn[s] # NoTitle
  /\ notedRev[s] = rev[attemptOn[s]]
  /\ onShelf[attemptOn[s]] < ShelfSize
  /\ rev[attemptOn[s]] < MaxRev
  /\ onShelf' = [onShelf EXCEPT ![attemptOn[s]] = @ + 1]
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![attemptOn[s]] = @ + 1]
  /\ attemptOn' = [attemptOn EXCEPT ![s] = NoTitle]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<notedRev, dead>>

ReRead(s) ==
  /\ s \notin dead
  /\ attemptOn[s] # NoTitle
  /\ notedRev[s] # rev[attemptOn[s]]
  /\ notedRev' = [notedRev EXCEPT ![s] = rev[attemptOn[s]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, rev, attemptOn, dead>>

AbandonFull(s) ==
  /\ s \notin dead
  /\ attemptOn[s] # NoTitle
  /\ \/ onShelf[attemptOn[s]] = ShelfSize
     \/ rev[attemptOn[s]] = MaxRev
  /\ attemptOn' = [attemptOn EXCEPT ![s] = NoTitle]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, rev, notedRev, dead>>

DieSilently(s) ==
  /\ s \notin dead
  /\ dead' = dead \cup {s}
  /\ attemptOn' = [attemptOn EXCEPT ![s] = NoTitle]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, rev, notedRev>>

BackInService(s) ==
  /\ s \in dead
  /\ dead' = dead \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, rev, attemptOn, notedRev>>

CancelHold(t) ==
  /\ onShelf[t] > 0
  /\ rev[t] < MaxRev
  /\ onShelf' = [onShelf EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<attemptOn, notedRev, dead>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Titles : CancelHold(t)
  \/ \E s \in Stations :
       \/ PostHold(s) \/ ReRead(s) \/ AbandonFull(s)
       \/ DieSilently(s) \/ BackInService(s)
       \/ \E t \in Titles : OpenAttempt(s, t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Stations = {branchWsA, branchWsB}
    Titles = {titleA, titleB}
    ShelfSize = 2
    Slack = 1
    MaxRev = 2
    NoTitle = noTitle
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ShelvesFitAndDeadStationsHoldNothing
nl:
A public library takes reservations on titles from workstations spread across its branches. Every title has a hold shelf behind the desk, and that shelf has a hard size: the number of copies the library is willing to keep off the open floor waiting for somebody to collect them. Beyond that size the shelf is full and no further hold may be placed on that title.

There is no lock on a title. A workstation opens an attempt against a title, notes the revision that title's hold record was on, and posts the hold only if the record is still on that revision; posting a hold advances the revision, which is what makes every other workstation's noted revision stale. A workstation whose noted revision has gone stale re-reads and works from the new one. A workstation whose title turns out to be full abandons the attempt rather than posting into a full shelf. Cancelling a hold takes a copy back off the shelf and also advances the revision.

Workstations die silently. A branch loses power, a terminal locks up, and the workstation simply stops -- there is no message and no partial write. This is the one place the library gets a free pass: an attempt that has not posted has changed nothing, so a workstation that dies takes its half-finished attempt with it and the hold record is untouched. What the library does insist on is that a dead workstation is never left holding an attempt in the record, because an attempt attributed to a terminal that is not running is an attempt nobody will ever finish or clean up. The branch supervisor brings dead workstations back into service.

The actions of the system are: a workstation opening an attempt against a title and noting its revision, a workstation posting a hold whose noted revision still matches onto a shelf that is under its size, a workstation re-reading a title whose revision moved under its attempt, a workstation abandoning an attempt against a title whose shelf is full, a workstation dying silently and taking its unposted attempt with it, the branch supervisor bringing a dead workstation back into service, and a hold being cancelled off a shelf.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No title's hold shelf ever holds more copies than its size, and no workstation that has died is left holding an attempt in the record.

---- MODULE W4Od7m3p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS GangOne, GangTwo, SlotCount, Slack, MaxShift, NoGang

Gangs == {GangOne, GangTwo}

ASSUME /\ GangOne # GangTwo
       /\ NoGang \notin Gangs
       /\ SlotCount \in Nat /\ SlotCount > 0
       /\ Slack \in Nat /\ Slack > 0
       /\ MaxShift \in Nat /\ MaxShift > 0

VARIABLES leader, shift, reserved, occupied, midSet

vars == <<leader, shift, reserved, occupied, midSet>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Gangs \cup {NoGang}
  /\ shift \in 0 .. MaxShift
  /\ reserved \in 0 .. SlotCount + Slack
  /\ occupied \in 0 .. SlotCount + Slack
  /\ midSet \subseteq Gangs

StackNeverOverCommitted == reserved + occupied <= SlotCount

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoGang
  /\ shift = 0
  /\ reserved = 0
  /\ occupied = 0
  /\ midSet = {}

ElectLeader(g) ==
  /\ leader = NoGang
  /\ leader' = g
  /\ shift' = IF shift < MaxShift THEN shift + 1 ELSE shift
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, occupied, midSet>>

LeaderStepsDown ==
  /\ leader # NoGang
  /\ leader' = NoGang
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shift, reserved, occupied, midSet>>

ReserveSlot ==
  /\ leader # NoGang
  /\ reserved + occupied < SlotCount
  /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, shift, occupied, midSet>>

BoxLands ==
  /\ reserved > 0
  /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
  /\ occupied' = occupied + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, shift, midSet>>

CraneLifts ==
  /\ occupied > 0
  /\ occupied' = occupied - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, shift, reserved, midSet>>

TakeOnWork(g) ==
  /\ g \notin midSet
  /\ midSet' = midSet \cup {g}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, shift, reserved, occupied>>

FinishWork(g) ==
  /\ g \in midSet
  /\ midSet' = midSet \ {g}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, shift, reserved, occupied>>

Next ==
  \/ LeaderStepsDown \/ ReserveSlot \/ BoxLands \/ CraneLifts
  \/ \E g \in Gangs : ElectLeader(g) \/ TakeOnWork(g) \/ FinishWork(g)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(FinishWork(GangOne))
  /\ WF_vars(FinishWork(GangTwo))

GangsAlwaysFinishTheirSet ==
  \A g \in Gangs : (g \in midSet) ~> (g \notin midSet)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    GangOne = lashGangOne
    GangTwo = lashGangTwo
    SlotCount = 3
    Slack = 1
    MaxShift = 2
    NoGang = noGang
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT StackNeverOverCommitted
PROPERTY GangsAlwaysFinishTheirSet
nl:
A container terminal works its quay stack through lashing gangs, and one gang at a time is the working leader for the berth. The gangs elect a leader and the election stamps a shift number on the winner, up to the highest number the berth log can carry for one shift. A leader that steps down leaves the berth without a leader until the next election; while the berth has no leader, nothing may be reserved.

The quay stack has a hard slot count -- the number of boxes that can stand alongside the crane without fouling the gantry rails. Working the stack goes in two steps. First the leader reserves a slot, which is a promise that a box is on its way and that nobody else may plan into that space. Then a box actually lands in the reserved slot, which converts the reservation into an occupied slot. Boxes also leave the stack when the crane lifts them aboard, freeing a slot outright. The terminal's rule is that reservations and occupied slots together never exceed the slot count, because a reservation that cannot be honoured is a box swinging over a full stack.

Gangs are slow, not absent. A gang that has taken on a piece of work stays on it for a while -- lashing rods do not come off quickly, and there is no way to hurry a gang that is mid-set. What matters is that the gang is still there and will finish; the terminal never has to write a gang off, only wait for it. A gang that is not mid-set can take on a new piece of work at any time.

The actions of the system are: electing a working leader for the berth and advancing the shift number, the leader stepping down and leaving the berth without one, the leader reserving a slot while reservations and occupied slots together are under the slot count, a box landing in a reserved slot and converting it to occupied, the crane lifting a box off the stack and freeing an occupied slot, a gang taking on a piece of work, and a gang finishing the piece of work it was on.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The reserved slots and the occupied slots on the quay stack never together exceed the stack's slot count.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A gang that has taken on a piece of work eventually finishes it and is no longer mid-set.

---- MODULE W4Od0m7p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Units, Rooms, Staffed, MaxGen, NoRoom

ASSUME /\ NoRoom \notin Rooms
       /\ Staffed \in Nat /\ Staffed > 0
       /\ MaxGen \in Nat /\ MaxGen > 0

VARIABLES bookedRooms, gen, names, carries

vars == <<bookedRooms, gen, names, carries>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ bookedRooms \subseteq Rooms
  /\ gen \in 0 .. MaxGen
  /\ names \in [Units -> Rooms \cup {NoRoom}]
  /\ carries \in [Units -> 0 .. MaxGen]

StillApplicable == {u \in Units : names[u] # NoRoom /\ carries[u] = gen}

BookingsFitAndApplicableRequestsAreFree ==
  /\ Cardinality(bookedRooms) <= Staffed
  /\ \A u \in StillApplicable : names[u] \notin bookedRooms

Init ==
  /\ bookedRooms = {}
  /\ gen = 0
  /\ names = [u \in Units |-> NoRoom]
  /\ carries = [u \in Units |-> 0]

PostRequest(u, m) ==
  /\ names[u] = NoRoom
  /\ m \notin bookedRooms
  /\ names' = [names EXCEPT ![u] = m]
  /\ carries' = [carries EXCEPT ![u] = gen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bookedRooms, gen>>

ApplyRequest(u) ==
  /\ names[u] # NoRoom
  /\ carries[u] = gen
  /\ gen < MaxGen
  /\ Cardinality(bookedRooms) < Staffed
  /\ bookedRooms' = bookedRooms \cup {names[u]}
  /\ gen' = gen + 1
  /\ names' = [names EXCEPT ![u] = NoRoom]
  /\ UNCHANGED carries

DropStale(u) ==
  /\ names[u] # NoRoom
  /\ carries[u] # gen
  /\ names' = [names EXCEPT ![u] = NoRoom]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bookedRooms, gen, carries>>

DropBlocked(u) ==
  /\ names[u] # NoRoom
  /\ carries[u] = gen
  /\ \/ Cardinality(bookedRooms) = Staffed
     \/ gen = MaxGen
  /\ names' = [names EXCEPT ![u] = NoRoom]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bookedRooms, gen, carries>>

CaseFinishes(m) ==
  /\ m \in bookedRooms
  /\ bookedRooms' = bookedRooms \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, names, carries>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Rooms : CaseFinishes(m)
  \/ \E u \in Units :
       \/ ApplyRequest(u) \/ DropStale(u) \/ DropBlocked(u)
       \/ \E m \in Rooms : PostRequest(u, m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Units = {surgUnitA, surgUnitB}
    Rooms = {orA, orB, orC}
    Staffed = 2
    MaxGen = 2
    NoRoom = noRoom
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BookingsFitAndApplicableRequestsAreFree
nl:
A hospital books its operating rooms through a single compare-and-swap register that carries a generation number. Requests to book a named room do not reach the register directly: they are posted onto the theatre message bus by the surgical units, and the bus reorders freely. A request that a unit posted first can be processed last, and there is no way for a unit to know where in the order its request will land.

Every posted request carries the room it names and the generation the register was on when the unit posted it. Applying a request is the compare-and-swap: it only takes if the register is still on the generation the request carries, and applying it books the named room and advances the generation. Advancing the generation is what invalidates every other request still sitting on the bus -- their carried generations no longer match, so they are stale and get dropped rather than applied. A unit whose request was dropped posts a fresh one.

The hospital will not staff more than a fixed number of rooms at once, so a request that arrives while that number is already booked is dropped rather than applied, and the unit tries again after a case finishes. Because a request is only ever posted against a room that is free at the moment of posting, and because applying one request makes every other outstanding request stale, no request that is still applicable can be pointing at a room that is already booked.

Cases finishing is a separate ledger operation, not a compare-and-swap: a booked room is released and becomes free again without touching the generation, because releasing a room can only make an outstanding request easier to satisfy, never harder.

The actions of the system are: a unit posting a request naming a room that is free at that moment and carrying the register's current generation, applying a request whose carried generation still matches and booking its room under the staffing number, dropping a request whose carried generation no longer matches, dropping a request that still matches but arrives with the staffing number already reached or the generation book exhausted, and a case finishing and releasing its room.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No more rooms are booked than the hospital staffs, and no request that is still applicable names a room that is already booked.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m3p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS DroneOne, DroneTwo, Directors, MaxRotation, NoDirector, NoDrone

Drones == {DroneOne, DroneTwo}

ASSUME /\ DroneOne # DroneTwo
       /\ NoDirector \notin Directors
       /\ NoDrone \notin Drones
       /\ MaxRotation \in Nat /\ MaxRotation > 0

VARIABLES director, rotation, corridor, cleared, phase, headsDown

vars == <<director, rotation, corridor, cleared, phase, headsDown>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ director \in Directors \cup {NoDirector}
  /\ rotation \in 0 .. MaxRotation
  /\ corridor \subseteq Drones
  /\ cleared \in Drones \cup {NoDrone}
  /\ phase \in [Drones -> {"holding", "descending"}]
  /\ headsDown \subseteq Directors

OnlyTheClearedDroneDescends ==
  /\ corridor \subseteq {cleared}
  /\ \A d \in corridor : phase[d] = "descending"

Init ==
  /\ director = NoDirector
  /\ rotation = 0
  /\ corridor = {}
  /\ cleared = NoDrone
  /\ phase = [d \in Drones |-> "holding"]
  /\ headsDown = {}

ElectDirector(f) ==
  /\ director = NoDirector
  /\ f \notin headsDown
  /\ director' = f
  /\ rotation' = IF rotation < MaxRotation THEN rotation + 1 ELSE rotation
  /\ UNCHANGED <<corridor, cleared, phase, headsDown>>

StandDown ==
  /\ director # NoDirector
  /\ director \notin headsDown
  /\ director' = NoDirector
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rotation, corridor, cleared, phase, headsDown>>

GoHeadsDown(f) ==
  /\ f \notin headsDown
  /\ headsDown' = headsDown \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<director, rotation, corridor, cleared, phase>>

ComeBackUp(f) ==
  /\ f \in headsDown
  /\ headsDown' = headsDown \ {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<director, rotation, corridor, cleared, phase>>

ClearDrone(d) ==
  /\ director # NoDirector
  /\ director \notin headsDown
  /\ corridor = {}
  /\ cleared = NoDrone
  /\ phase[d] = "holding"
  /\ cleared' = d
  /\ UNCHANGED <<director, rotation, corridor, phase, headsDown>>

EnterCorridor(d) ==
  /\ cleared = d
  /\ corridor = {}
  /\ phase[d] = "holding"
  /\ corridor' = {d}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "descending"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<director, rotation, cleared, headsDown>>

LeaveCorridor(d) ==
  /\ d \in corridor
  /\ corridor' = corridor \ {d}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "holding"]
  /\ cleared' = NoDrone
  /\ UNCHANGED <<director, rotation, headsDown>>

Next ==
  \/ StandDown
  \/ \E f \in Directors : ElectDirector(f) \/ GoHeadsDown(f) \/ ComeBackUp(f)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : ClearDrone(d) \/ EnterCorridor(d) \/ LeaveCorridor(d)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(LeaveCorridor(DroneOne))
  /\ WF_vars(LeaveCorridor(DroneTwo))

CorridorAlwaysClears ==
  \A d \in Drones : (d \in corridor) ~> (d \notin corridor)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    DroneOne = tankerOne
    DroneTwo = tankerTwo
    Directors = {fltDirA, fltDirB}
    MaxRotation = 2
    NoDirector = noDirector
    NoDrone = noDrone
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheClearedDroneDescends
PROPERTY CorridorAlwaysClears
nl:
A wildfire drone swarm drops retardant through a single descent corridor cut into the smoke column. The corridor takes one aircraft at a time: two drones descending it together in nil visibility is the accident the whole deconfliction scheme exists to prevent. Which drone may use it is decided by a flight director, and the swarm elects one director at a time, the election stamping a rotation number on the winner up to the highest number the sortie log carries.

A director that stands down leaves the swarm without one, and while there is no director nobody may be cleared into the corridor. Directors do not vanish, though -- they go heads-down. A director working a hand-off, or talking to the air attack supervisor on another frequency, is slow rather than absent: it will answer, just not now, and while it is heads-down it cannot issue a clearance or stand down. The swarm never has to write a director off, only wait for one to come back up.

Every drone is either holding above the column or descending the corridor. A director clears exactly one holding drone at a time, and only when the corridor is empty. The cleared drone enters the corridor and switches from holding to descending. When it comes off the bottom of the corridor it goes back to holding, the corridor is empty again, and the clearance is torn up so that the next drone needs a fresh one.

The actions of the system are: electing a flight director and advancing the rotation number, a director standing down and leaving the swarm without one, a director going heads-down, a heads-down director coming back up, a director that is up clearing a holding drone into an empty corridor, the cleared drone entering the corridor and switching to descending, and a descending drone coming off the bottom of the corridor, going back to holding and having its clearance torn up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of drones in the descent corridor is always contained in the set containing just the drone that currently holds a clearance, and every drone in the corridor is in the descending state.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A drone that has entered the descent corridor eventually leaves it.
